A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ActiveGAMER paper and complete supplementary material. All 19 pages, including equations, Algorithm 1, Tables 1–7 and Figures 1–9, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction and rendering experiments on Replica and MP3D, ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary per-scene results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same Gaussian mapping, rendering-based planning, coarse-to-fine exploration, global-local keyframe selection and post-refinement procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight Replica scenes and five MP3D scenes for reconstruction and novel-view rendering. Supplementary trajectories and failure scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FBE, UPEN, OccAnt, ANM and NARUTO; Table 2 retains SplaTAM and NARUTO. Comparator membership also matches in supplementary Tables 5–7.

E3.justification: Both retain the 2000/5000-step budgets, 680 × 1200 RGB-D inputs, geometric and rendering metrics, and evaluation procedures. SplaTAM's disabled tracking and evaluation masking, along with supplementary circular viewing trajectories, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The exploration, global-keyframe and post-refinement ablations in Section 4.3 and Table 3 are identical. Figure 5 and the supplementary runtime, trajectory and failure-case analyses are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains the same information-gain distribution display, and Section 8 retains the same average-runtime reporting. There are no changes to run-count, seed, uncertainty or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and the plotted and qualitative results match. For example, average PSNR remains 32.02 dB on Replica in Table 2 and 24.76 dB on MP3D in Table 7.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same Gaussian representation, rendering formulas, optimization loss, densification rule and information-gain definition. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and Section 5 retain the same claims about efficient Gaussian-based active mapping, unrestricted 6DoF exploration and geometric and photometric performance.

C2.justification: Both retain the rendering-quality versus geometric-completeness tradeoff and the same limitations concerning known localization, perfect action execution, motion constraints, near-surface sampling and double-sided objects.

D1.justification: Section 7 retains the same CPU/V100 hardware, memory figures, 15/60 optimization iterations and quarter/full-resolution densification details. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 76 references match, including the positioning relative to NARUTO, ActiveSplat and AG-SLAM.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v2, 1 Apr 2025 to v3, 4 Sep 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology and section organization otherwise remain unchanged; extracted whitespace differences do not represent rewritten content.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–7 and Algorithm 1 retain their graphics, captions, structure and placement. Rendered-page comparison establishes no figure, table or layout revision.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, numerical evidence, supplementary analyses, reproducibility details and limitations are unchanged. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp does not meaningfully alter the paper's clarity, evidential support or overall quality.
